ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The radius R of the large roller of a road roller is twice the radius r of the small roller. When the road roller travels at a uniform speed, the centripetal acceleration of point A on the edge of the large roller is $0.12 \mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the centripetal acceleration of point B on the edge of the small roller?
2. What is the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration of point C on the large roller, which is at a distance of $\frac{R}{3}$ from its axis?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The radius R of the large roller of a road roller is twice the radius r of the small roller. When the road roller travels at a uniform speed, the centripetal acceleration of point A on the edge of the large roller is $0.12 \,\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. What is the centripetal acceleration of point B on the edge of the small roller? 2. What is the magnitude of the centripetal acceleration of point C on the large roller, which is at a distance of $\frac{R}{3}$ from its axis?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a road roller; at the rear right there is a relatively large roller, labeled with radius R; on the lower right side of the edge of the large roller there is a point A marked; inside the large roller along the radial direction there is a point C; at the front left there is a relatively small roller, labeled with radius r, and near the edge of the small roller there is a point B marked. The problem states that the radius R of the large roller is 2 times the radius r of the small roller, namely R=2r, and that the centripetal acceleration of point A on the edge of the large roller is 0.12 cm/s^2. Reasoning: When the road roller rolls purely at uniform speed, the large and small rollers have the same translational speed v. The angular velocity of the large roller is omega_large=v/R, and the angular velocity of the small roller is omega_small=v/r. Point A is on the edge of the large roller, and its centripetal acceleration is a_A=omega_large^2 R=v^2/R=0.12 cm/s^2. Point B is on the edge of the small roller, so a_B=omega_small^2 r=v^2/r. Since R=2r, v^2/r=2v^2/R=2a_A=0.24 cm/s^2. Point C is located on the large roller, at a distance R/3 from the axis, and has the same angular velocity as the large roller, therefore a_C=omega_large^2(R/3)=(omega_large^2 R)/3=a_A/3=0.04 cm/s^2.
